about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data: the shipped playbook with a hook on its attack (docs/agents/add_finish.py; DESIGN.md section 34). Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Version 2 (candidate 'answers') = the shipped version 1 (its trigger rules and its twelve cast rules unchanged and in their order, now rules 1-3 and 9-17; no attack block, Forge attacks, as shipped) with five rules, 4 to 8, for the deck's edicts and sweepers, which version 1 left to Forge. Written from the 200 games of the league of twelve (league-run #3, seed 20261250), where the seat won 37, lost 162 and was first out in 68. Games drawn / cast / in hand on the seat's last turn of a loss: Syphon Flesh 44/16/23, Fleshbag Marauder 51/26/19, Mutilate 48/7/31, Necrotic Hex 57/12/35, Noxious Ghoul 41/7/29; on own turns with the card in hand and lands >= its mana value they sat 134, 174, 193, 124 and 190 times. The targeted removal (Go for the Throat, Consuming Corruption, Tendrils of Corruption, Withering Torment, Consumed by Greed) is cast by Forge in most games it is drawn and was in hand at 1 to 4 losses each: left to Forge, which picks the targets a rule could not. They sit after the rocks, Gisa and Gisa's activation (so Gisa makes her tokens before a sacrifice effect asks for six creatures) and before the lords and creatures. Rule 4, Noxious Ghoul with an opponent at 3+ creatures: the deck's one-sided sweeper (-1/-1 to non-Zombies for every Zombie that enters), first so the Zombies cast after it in the same turn trigger it; it also shrinks Gisa, Kalitas, Ayara and Grave Titan. Rule 5, Syphon Flesh whenever an opponent has a creature: one-sided, each other player sacrifices one and we get a Zombie for each. Rule 6, Necrotic Hex with an opponent at 3+ creatures: every player sacrifices six and we alone get six 2/2 Zombies back, so it is near one-sided for a deck of tokens. Rule 7, Mutilate (-1/-1 per Swamp to every creature, ours too) only when behind: 5+ lands, an opponent with 3+ creatures and more power than our whole board. Rule 8, Fleshbag Marauder whenever an opponent has a creature: each player sacrifices one, and Forge gives up our lowest-rated creature, usually a token or the Marauder itself. The seat's losses there came by combat (7,607 of 8,030 damage taken in the last four game turns), a median of four attackers at it per attack. Checked at 16 local tables of bots (seeds 20263060 and 20263061): the five rules fired 16 times, Syphon Flesh 4 casts (11 opposing creatures sacrificed, 13 tokens), Fleshbag Marauder 4, Necrotic Hex 2 (18 opposing creatures and 7 of ours gone, 12 tokens), Noxious Ghoul 3 (3 opposing creatures killed in all, two casts killed none: the -1/-1 only kills X/1s unless more Zombies follow), Mutilate 1 (at 8 life: 8 of theirs, 1 of ours) and held through five turns of a game the seat was ahead in and won. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #32: on the same 200 tables of bots (seed 20261300, opponents drawn from the other eleven bots under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) it won 38 against version 1's 27 (+5.5 points, 95% +0 to +11, exact test 0.061); the cards the new rules name were cast in 190 of the 247 games they were drawn, under version 1 in 61 of 248. It has not been set against its stock pilot. What it still casts in a share of games 15 points or more below stock AI's (the stock arm of ab-run #26, other tables of the same pool), 8 cards: Graveborn Muse, Marchesa's Decree, Soulless One, Sign in Blood, Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet, Josu Vess, Lich Knight and 2 more (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/pool-answers/wretched-ranks-check.txt). VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `hooksopen` (2026-11-21). Version 2 with five changes: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); and then a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); and then when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). No cast or trigger rule is changed.
